standard.title: Decimals beyond hundredths
standard.description: Interpret, compare and order numbers with more than 2 decimal places, including numbers greater than one, using place value understanding; represent these on a number line
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can represent and compare decimals to hundredths on a number line (AC9M4N01). They have not yet interpreted thousandths or beyond, or compared decimals greater than one requiring more than 2 decimal places.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret, compare and order numbers with more than 2 decimal places, including numbers greater than one, using place value understanding, and represent these on a number line.

nodes.label: Tenths and hundredths review
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can name the place value of each digit in a decimal to hundredths and explain what each digit represents.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and name the value of each digit in a decimal number to hundredths (e.g. 3.47 — 3 ones, 4 tenths, 7 hundredths).
nodes.typical_width: Represent and interpret decimals to hundredths using place value charts, number lines and MAB-style representations; explain the relative size of tenths and hundredths.
wider: Use measurement contexts (e.g. metres/centimetres) to ground place value meaning
success_criteria: Student correctly identifies the place value of each digit in a given decimal to hundredths
Student can partition a decimal to hundredths into its component parts and record them

nodes.label: Thousandths and beyond
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read, write and name decimals with more than 2 decimal places, explaining the place value of each digit.
nodes.minimum_width: Read, write and name a decimal to thousandths; identify the place value of each digit.
nodes.typical_width: Extend the place value chart to thousandths and ten-thousandths; connect to metric contexts (e.g. kilometres, millimetres). Explain the pattern of powers of ten extending to the right.
wider: Explore scientific measurement contexts requiring 4+ decimal places
Investigate how First Nations land measurement and navigation systems express precision differently

response_modes.reason: Thousandths are abstract without grounding contexts. Students commonly confuse the length of a decimal with its magnitude — more decimal places perceived as bigger. Multiple concrete contexts (measurement, money, science) help resolve this.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Rich measurement contexts (km, scientific data) provide genuine breadth and relevance for advancing students.
nodes.hinge_reason: The 'longer decimal = bigger number' misconception causes systematic errors in Node 3 — students who conflate decimal length with magnitude cannot compare or order decimals correctly.
success_criteria: Student reads and writes a decimal to thousandths correctly
Student identifies the place value of each digit in a decimal with 3+ decimal places

nodes.label: Comparing and ordering decimals
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare and order sets of decimals with more than 2 decimal places, including decimals greater than one, justifying their reasoning using place value.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare two decimals with up to 3 decimal places and place them in order, justifying using place value column comparison.
nodes.typical_width: Order sets of 4-6 decimals with mixed decimal places (e.g. 1.3, 0.27, 1.039, 0.3); explain common ordering errors (e.g. treating longer decimals as larger).
wider: Compare decimals arising from measurement contexts with different units requiring conversion
Sort sporting or scientific data (e.g. race times, pH values) where ordering decimals is purposeful
Explore how different representations (number line, place value chart) highlight different aspects of comparison

response_modes.reason: The 'longer decimal = bigger number' misconception is persistent. Varied contexts expose the misconception from multiple angles — students who see only abstract lists may retain the error even after instruction.
Comparison requires consistent application of the place value alignment procedure. Students benefit from practising the alignment step explicitly before it becomes fluent.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Sports and science datasets give purposeful, rich ordering tasks for advancing students.
nodes.hinge_reason: Accurate decimal comparison is the prerequisite for number line placement in Node 4 — students who cannot correctly order decimals cannot meaningfully position them on a number line.
success_criteria: Student correctly orders a set of decimals with different numbers of decimal places
Student identifies and explains the error in an incorrect ordering (e.g. 0.35 > 0.9)

nodes.label: Representing on a number line
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can place decimals with more than 2 decimal places, including numbers greater than one, accurately on a number line.
nodes.minimum_width: Place at least two decimals with 3 decimal places on a labelled number line, choosing an appropriate scale.
nodes.typical_width: Construct and label a number line for a given range and interval; place decimals greater than one and justify placement using place value estimation.
wider: Use open number lines to compare intervals between decimals
Connect to measurement scales (thermometers, rulers, scales) as physical number lines

response_modes.reason: Accurate number line placement requires students to apply both understanding (place value) and precision (estimation of intervals). Fluency here supports all subsequent decimal work.

success_criteria: Student places given decimals with 3+ decimal places on a number line at approximately correct positions
Student justifies placement using place value language
